prompts.security-review: Review Courier's web app and API for security problems.
prompts.code-review: Review Courier's code for bugs and problems.
prompts.compliance-review: Review Courier for data protection and card payment compliance problems. It operates in the United Kingdom.
prompts.contract-check: Check that Courier's API does what its OpenAPI contract says.
prompts.accessibility-review: Review Courier's web app for accessibility problems.
prompts.performance-review: Review Courier's API and database for performance problems.
prompts.reliability-review: Review Courier's API for reliability problems.

defects.title: The session signing key is written in the code
Any website may call the API with a signed-in customer's credentials
The status filter is pasted into SQL, so it can be used for SQL injection
Any signed-in customer can read another customer's parcel

locations.match: "SELECT id, status, weight_kg, recipient_name, recipient_address, notes FROM parcels WHERE id = %s",

defects.title: Booking writes the recipient's name, phone and address to the logs
Booking returns recipientName, where the contract promises recipient_name
Listing parcels returns every one a customer ever booked, with no limit or paging

locations.match: return db.execute(query + " ORDER BY created_at DESC").fetchall()

defects.title: Public tracking shows the recipient's name and address to anyone with the link

locations.match: "SELECT status, recipient_name, recipient_address FROM parcels WHERE tracking_code = %s",

defects.title: Full card numbers and CVVs are received and stored

locations.match: "INSERT INTO payments (parcel_id, customer_id, card_number, expiry, cvv, amount_pence) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)",

defects.title: The customer's browser decides how much to pay
The geocoding call has no timeout, so a slow provider hangs bookings
Parcels are looked up by customer with no index on customer_id

locations.match:
customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id),
  tracking_code

defects.title: A migration drops customers' parcel notes, which the API still reads and writes

locations.match: ALTER TABLE parcels DROP COLUMN notes;

defects.title: Prices are worked out in pounds as decimals, while the API charges whole pence
Parcel notes are put into the page as HTML, so they can run a script
A parcel's status is shown only as a colour
The booking form's fields have no labels, only placeholders
Session tokens never expire and can't be revoked
